kept.q: Which of the following correctly represents the laboratory preparation of chlorine gas by the oxidation of concentrated hydrochloric acid with manganese(IV) oxide?
options: MnO2 + 4HCl -> MnCl2 + Cl2 + 2H2O
MnO2 + 2HCl -> MnCl2 + H2O2
MnO2 + 4HCl -> MnCl4 + 2H2O
Mn + 4HCl -> MnCl4 + 2H2
kept.explanation: Manganese(IV) oxide oxidises concentrated hydrochloric acid to chlorine gas while it is itself reduced to manganese(II) chloride, with water as the other product. The equation must balance atoms and charge, which only the first option does correctly.

kept.q: 0.80 g of a metal M reacts completely with excess dilute tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid to liberate 0.02 mol of hydrogen gas according to the equation: M + H2SO4 -> MSO4 + H2. What is the relative atomic mass of M?
kept.explanation: From the equation, 1 mole of M produces 1 mole of hydrogen gas, so 0.02 mol of M reacted. Relative atomic mass equals mass divided by moles: 0.80 g divided by 0.02 mol gives 40.
kept.pidgin: From the equation, 1 mole of M dey produce 1 mole of hydrogen gas, meaning 0.02 mol of M react. If you divide 0.80 g by 0.02 mol, you go get 40 as the relative atomic mass.

kept.q: A gaseous mixture contains nitrogen and hydrogen in the mole ratio 1:3, the exact ratio required for the Haber process. If 5 moles of nitrogen react completely with the available hydrogen and the reaction proceeds at 40% yield, how many moles of ammonia are formed? (N2 + 3H2 -> 2NH3)
kept.explanation: At complete reaction, 5 moles of nitrogen would give 10 moles of ammonia based on the mole ratio in the equation. At 40% yield, the actual amount formed is 40% of 10, which is 4.0 moles.
kept.pidgin: If the reaction go 100%, 5 moles of nitrogen suppose produce 10 moles of ammonia. But as the yield na 40%, you go multiply 10 by 0.4 to get 4.0 moles.

q.q: A student bubbles hydrogen sulphide gas into a solution of iron(III) chloride. Which of the following best describes what happens?
options: The iron(III) ions are reduced to iron(II) ions as a pale yellow precipitate of sulphur forms
The iron(III) ions are oxidised to iron(IV) ions as hydrogen gas is liberated
No reaction occurs because hydrogen sulphide is a weak reducing agent
A black precipitate of iron(III) sulphide forms and chlorine gas is released
NONEOFTHEABOVE
q.explanation: Hydrogen sulphide is a strong reducing agent; it reduces iron(III) ions to iron(II) ions while itself being oxidised to elemental sulphur, which appears as a pale yellow or cloudy precipitate. This is a classic redox reaction used to identify reducing gases.

q.q: In the contact process for manufacturing tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid, what is the main reason vanadium(V) oxide is used in the reaction chamber?
options: It acts as a catalyst to speed up the attainment of equilibrium without being consumed
It reacts with sulphur(IV) oxide to directly form the acid
It absorbs sulphur(VI) oxide to form oleum
It lowers the temperature needed for the reaction to proceed
NONEOFTHEABOVE
q.explanation: Vanadium(V) oxide serves as the catalyst in the contact process, increasing the rate at which sulphur(IV) oxide is oxidised to sulphur(VI) oxide without itself being used up. It does not take part permanently in the reaction.

q.q: A sample of ammonia gas is tested by holding a glass rod dipped in concentrated hydrochloric acid near the mouth of the gas jar. What is observed, and what does it confirm?
options: Dense white fumes form, confirming the presence of ammonia gas
A colourless gas is released with no visible change, confirming the gas is pure hydrogen
A brown gas forms, confirming the presence of nitrogen(IV) oxide
The litmus paper turns red, confirming the gas is acidic
NONEOFTHEABOVE
q.explanation: Ammonia reacts with hydrogen chloride vapour from concentrated hydrochloric acid to form solid ammonium chloride, seen as dense white fumes. This is a standard confirmatory test for ammonia gas.

q.q: Which pair of properties correctly describes the gas produced when zinc trioxocarbonate(IV) is heated and the resulting gas is passed through limewater?
options: The gas is carbon(IV) oxide and it turns limewater milky
The gas is oxygen and it relights a glowing splint
The gas is carbon(II) oxide and it has no effect on limewater
The gas is hydrogen and it burns with a pop sound
NONEOFTHEABOVE
q.explanation: Heating zinc trioxocarbonate(IV) decomposes it into zinc oxide and carbon(IV) oxide gas. Carbon(IV) oxide turns limewater milky due to the formation of insoluble calcium trioxocarbonate(IV).

q.q: Which of the following statements correctly explains why concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid cannot be used to dry hydrogen sulphide gas during its laboratory preparation?
options: It oxidises the hydrogen sulphide gas to sulphur and sulphur(IV) oxide
It reacts with hydrogen sulphide to form a soluble salt
It is too weak an acid to absorb moisture from the gas
It forms a precipitate that blocks the delivery tube
NONEOFTHEABOVE
q.explanation: Concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid is a strong oxidising agent and will oxidise hydrogen sulphide, a reducing gas, to sulphur and sulphur(IV) oxide instead of simply drying it. This redox reaction makes it unsuitable as a drying agent for this particular gas.
